name: sidebar-header-and-folder-geometry
description:
Three sidebar chrome geometry checks sharing one fixture, since the dom-shim has no layout and each needs a real VM frame.

the fixture carries two folders (News, Sports) so 'the next row' after the first folder's last row is the SECOND folder's own head - a real .row element, not the Tabs section header or the New Tab button that would otherwise sit between a single folder and the plain rows below it. .scrollinner and .rows both carry a flat 4px gap (commit 98407918fe1f6 dropped the old -6px .fold margin that used to cancel a 10px section gap down to that same 4px); the eval compares the two gaps directly rather than asserting a literal pixel count, so it survives either value moving in lockstep later.

the fixture's two plain tabs (Plain One, Plain Two) also answer the row-gap half of the check on their own, so one fixture covers both. The offset eval reads the vertical centre of .wsic (the space name's icon slot) against the space name label's own centre.

the fixture's single space still renders through buildRail (the >=1 threshold), so its .spacedots bar sits beside .rail rather than inside .sidebar - the DOM position where .sidebar button's cursor:inherit override cannot reach a .sdot's own cursor rule.

actions.note: gate: the first grouped tab committed, so the space and its folders are live
let the sidebar model arrive and the rail render both folders and the plain rows

actions.expression: (() => { const frow1 = document.querySelector('.row.frow'); const fold1 = frow1.nextElementSibling; const rows = fold1.querySelectorAll('.tabrow'); const lastFolderRow = rows[rows.length - 1]; const nextRow = fold1.nextElementSibling; const plainRows = document.querySelectorAll('.rows > .tabrow'); const folderGap = nextRow.getBoundingClientRect().top - lastFolderRow.getBoundingClientRect().bottom; const rowGap = plainRows[1].getBoundingClientRect().top - plainRows[0].getBoundingClientRect().bottom; return String(Math.round(folderGap) === Math.round(rowGap)); })()
actions.note: the gap from the first folder's last row to the second folder's head, against the gap between the two plain rows

actions.expression: (() => { const frow1 = document.querySelector('.row.frow'); const fold1 = frow1.nextElementSibling; const rows = fold1.querySelectorAll('.tabrow'); const lastFolderRow = rows[rows.length - 1]; const nextRow = fold1.nextElementSibling; const plainRows = document.querySelectorAll('.rows > .tabrow'); const folderGap = nextRow.getBoundingClientRect().top - lastFolderRow.getBoundingClientRect().bottom; const rowGap = plainRows[1].getBoundingClientRect().top - plainRows[0].getBoundingClientRect().bottom; return folderGap.toFixed(2) + ' vs ' + rowGap.toFixed(2); })()
actions.note: RECORDED, NOT ASSERTED: the raw gaps folder-gap-matches-row-gap only compares as rounded booleans - kept so a mismatch names the actual pixel drift instead of just failing

actions.expression: (() => { const dot = document.querySelector('.wsic'); const label = document.querySelector('.wsname span:last-child'); const d = dot.getBoundingClientRect(); const l = label.getBoundingClientRect(); const dotCenter = d.top + d.height / 2; const labelCenter = l.top + l.height / 2; return String(Math.abs(dotCenter - labelCenter) < 1); })()
actions.note: the space icon's vertical centre against the space name's, under 1px apart

actions.expression: (() => { const dot = document.querySelector('.sdot'); return dot ? getComputedStyle(dot).cursor : 'MISSING'; })()
actions.note: the space dot's own computed cursor, read where the rail actually renders it - beside .rail, not inside .sidebar

actions.expression: (() => { const gap = (frow) => { const fold = frow.nextElementSibling; return Math.round(fold.getBoundingClientRect().top - frow.getBoundingClientRect().bottom); }; const rows = document.querySelectorAll('.folderlist > .frow'); return rows[0].dataset.folderId.slice(0, 4) + ':' + gap(rows[0]) + ' ' + rows[1].dataset.folderId.slice(0, 4) + ':' + gap(rows[1]); })()
actions.note: Review: .folderlist > .fold + .frow only spaces one folder's END from the NEXT folder's head - a folder's OWN head-to-body gap (frow immediately followed by its own fold, the opposite sibling order) must stay 0, or the fix leaked a stray band under every header
both folders open, for the eye

actions.expression: (() => { const frow = [...document.querySelectorAll('.folderlist > .frow')].find((f) => f.dataset.folderId === '22222222-7477-4774-8774-747747747747'); frow.click(); return frow.classList.contains('closedH') ? 'closing' : 'no-toggle'; })()
actions.note: the delegated .frow click handler toggles the folder - not an OS-level hit-test like the nav row, so a DOM click is the real path here

actions.expression: (() => { const gap = (frow) => { const fold = frow.nextElementSibling; return Math.round(fold.getBoundingClientRect().top - frow.getBoundingClientRect().bottom); }; const rows = document.querySelectorAll('.folderlist > .frow'); return rows[0].dataset.folderId.slice(0, 4) + ':' + gap(rows[0]) + ' ' + rows[1].dataset.folderId.slice(0, 4) + ':' + gap(rows[1]); })()
actions.note: re-measured with Sports collapsed: its own head-to-body gap must still read 0, same as News's, open or closed
Sports collapsed, News still open, for the eye

assertions.note: the folder's bottom gap equals the plain-row gap
icon and name share one vertical centre, within 1px
the space dot keeps the sidebar's default arrow, not a pointer hand
Review: the .fold + .frow fix must not touch a folder's own head-to-body gap
Review: same guarantee with Sports collapsed - no stray band appears under a closed header either
